about: Where JavaScript's regex engine (flag i, no u) and Python's re (re.ASCII | re.IGNORECASE, \s compiled as JavaScript's whitespace class) could differ. `expect` is what check() reports after normalize(); `expect_raw`, where present, is what the compiled rules report over the text as given (the engines alone, checked by both suites through check_raw/checkRaw), and defaults to `expect`. Cases with `expect` must agree; the one case with `expect_js`/`expect_py` is the documented divergence. Written with \u escapes so no invisible character hides in the file.

cases.note: U+FEFF is in JavaScript's \s (expect_raw); normalize removes it as a zero-width character, so the text reads `moves.Not` and contrast/3's sentence break is gone
U+001C is Python str whitespace but not JavaScript's \s; the compiled class follows JavaScript
\b is ASCII in both: é is not a word character, so there is a boundary before w
long s does not case-fold to s in either engine (expect_raw); NFKC makes it s, so normalize catches it
Kelvin sign does not case-fold to k in either engine (expect_raw); NFKC makes it K, so normalize catches it
a curly apostrophe reads as the straight one SPEC's patterns spell after normalize (expect_raw: the engines alone do not)
the same, U+2019 after normalize (expect_raw: the engines alone do not)
the same, U+2018 after normalize (expect_raw: the engines alone do not)
THE ONE KNOWN DIVERGENCE: {0,40} counts UTF-16 units in JavaScript (1 + 42 here, over the bound) and code points in Python (1 + 21, within it).
